## Purpose

This SOP defines the protocols for extraction verification, instrument
parameters, operation, and safety requirements for analyzing trace
pesticide residues using Gas Chromatography (GC) coupled with
specialized detectors (ECD or MS) [@usepa8081b; @mcnair2019].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Targeted pesticide residue analysis in environmental
  water, soil extracts, and plant tissue digests using GC-ECD or GC-MS
- **Does not apply to:** LC-amenable pesticides, non-targeted screening,
  or preparative-scale separations
- **Location:** Environmental analysis laboratories


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Autosampler:** A robotic device that withdraws a precise volume
  from each GC vial and injects it into the inlet without manual
  intervention; reduces injection variability and allows unattended
  overnight sequences.
- **Capillary column:** A fused-silica column (typically 15--60 m ×
  0.18--0.32 mm ID) coated on its interior with a thin film of
  stationary phase; separates pesticides by their differential
  affinity for the stationary phase relative to the carrier gas
  [@mcnair2019].
- **Carrier gas:** An inert gas (helium, nitrogen, or hydrogen) that
  moves sample vapor through the column; flow rate and mode (constant
  pressure or constant flow) affect retention times and peak shape
  [@mcnair2019].
- **CCV (continuing calibration verification) standard:** A
  mid-range calibration standard analyzed every 10 injections to
  confirm that instrument response has not drifted; must recover
  within ±15% of the true value [@usepa8081b].
- **Column bleed:** Gradual decomposition and volatilization of the
  GC stationary phase at high temperature; produces a rising baseline
  at the end of a temperature program; distinguished from analyte
  peaks by reproducible retention and broad peak shape.
- **ECD (electron capture detector):** A selective detector that
  measures current suppression caused by electron-capturing
  compounds (organochlorine pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls);
  extremely sensitive (pg range) for halogenated compounds
  [@usepa8081b].
- **GC-MS (gas chromatography-mass spectrometry):** Coupling of a
  GC with a mass spectrometer; provides compound identification by
  mass spectrum matching in addition to retention time; the
  confirmatory technique for pesticide analysis [@usepa8270e].
- **Inlet liner:** A deactivated glass tube inside the split/splitless
  inlet; protects the column from non-volatile matrix residues;
  replaced daily or after every 50--100 injections to prevent sample
  carry-over and peak degradation.
- **MDL (method detection limit):** The minimum analyte concentration
  that can be detected with 99% confidence under the stated method
  conditions; determined from replicate analyses of low-level
  standards; listed per analyte in the method SOP.
- **RPD (relative percent difference):** |A - B| / ((A + B) / 2) × 100;
  used to assess duplicate precision; acceptance criterion is RPD
  ≤ 20% for environmental matrices [@usepa8081b].
- **Septum:** A silicone or PTFE-faced silicone disc that seals the
  inlet and is penetrated by the autosampler needle; replaced daily
  or after 50--100 injections to prevent coring fragments from
  entering the liner.
- **Splitless injection mode:** An inlet mode in which the split vent
  is closed during injection to transfer nearly all of the sample
  onto the column; standard for trace pesticide analysis to maximize
  sensitivity [@mcnair2019].
- **Standby method:** A GC method programmed after sequence
  completion that drops oven, inlet, and detector temperatures while
  maintaining a reduced carrier gas flow; prevents column oxidation
  and extends stationary phase lifetime.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical toxicity:** Pesticide standards, target analytes, and
  extraction solvents (hexane, dichloromethane, acetone) are highly
  toxic, carcinogenic, or neurotoxic. Inhalation of vapors or skin
  absorption poses a severe chronic health risk.
- **Thermal:** The GC injection port (200--250 °C) and column oven
  (50--320 °C) operate at extreme temperatures causing instant severe
  burns. Ensure the inlet is below 50 °C before opening it.
- **High-pressure gas cylinders:** Carrier gas cylinders (helium,
  nitrogen, hydrogen) pose crush and high-pressure hazards if dropped
  or if regulators fail. Hydrogen carrier gas presents an explosion
  risk if allowed to accumulate in the oven.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or chemical splash goggles
- [ ] Laboratory coat (fully fastened)
- [ ] Nitrile or solvent-resistant gloves (Viton or Silver Shield for
      bulk chlorinated solvents)

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chemical spill, gas leak, or equipment failure, refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) or call
campus safety. For compressed gas emergencies, evacuate the area and
contact EH&S.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                           | Notes                                      |
|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Gas chromatograph              | With autosampler, split/splitless capillary inlet, and detector (ECD or MS) |
| Fused-silica capillary column  | e.g., 30 m × 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film, semi-volatile optimized [@mcnair2019] |
| Carrier gas cylinders          | Helium or nitrogen (carrier); nitrogen (ECD makeup) |
| Inline gas traps               | Moisture, oxygen, and hydrocarbon traps    |

### Consumables

| Item                              | Notes                                   |
|:----------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| GC vials (2 mL amber glass)       | With PTFE-lined septa [@mcnair2019]     |
| Replacement injection port liners | Deactivated split/splitless with quartz wool plug |
| Low-bleed septa                   | Replace daily or every 50--100 injections |
| Certified pesticide reference standards | Spanning expected concentration range [@usepa8081b] |
| Extraction solvents               | Hexane, dichloromethane, acetone (GC grade) |


## Procedure

### Gas Cylinder and Inlet Verification

1. Verify carrier gas cylinders have sufficient pressure (> 500 psi).
2. Confirm secondary regulator delivery pressure meets manufacturer
   specifications (typically 60--80 psi).
3. Check moisture, oxygen, and hydrocarbon traps; replace if indicator
   dyes signal saturation.

### Injection Port Maintenance (Pre-Run Check)

::: {.callout-important}
### Hot Inlet
Ensure the inlet temperature has dropped below 50 °C before opening
the inlet assembly.
:::

1. Replace the injection port septum daily or every 50--100 injections
   [@mcnair2019].
2. Inspect the glass liner; replace if charring, particulate matter,
   or matrix deposits are visible.

### Sequence Setup and Sample Loading

1. Prepare calibration curves from certified pesticide reference
   materials spanning expected concentration intervals (e.g.,
   10--1000 µg/L) [@usepa8081b].
2. Aliquot extracts into clean 2 mL amber GC vials; cap with
   PTFE-faced septa.
3. Program the injection sequence including:
   - Solvent blanks (hexane/acetone matrix check)
   - Multi-point calibration curve
   - CCV standards every 10 injections
   - Duplicate sample matrices

### Initiating the GC Run

1. Load the analytical method and verify parameters [@usepa8081b]:
   - **Inlet:** Splitless mode; 250 °C
   - **Oven program:** 50 °C (1 min hold) → ramp 10 °C/min → 300 °C
     (5 min hold)
   - **Carrier gas:** Constant flow, 1.2 mL/min helium
2. Allow all zones to reach setpoint; confirm `Ready` status in
   software.
3. Initiate the sequence; monitor the first injection cycle to confirm
   the autosampler syringe articulates without bending the needle.

### Post-Analysis and Standby Shutdown

1. Review chromatogram baselines for peak symmetry, column bleed
   spikes, or retention time shifts.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Retention Time Drift
If retention times shift, trimming 10--20 cm from the front of the
analytical column can restore performance. Document the trim in the
instrument logbook [@mcnair2019].
:::

2. Upon sequence completion, load the Standby method to drop oven and
   detector temperatures while maintaining a reduced carrier gas purge
   to prevent column phase oxidation.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Initial calibration: $r^2 \geq 0.995$ [@usepa8081b].
- CCV standards every 10 injections: recovery within ±15%; halt and
  re-calibrate if outside this window [@usepa8081b].
- Method blanks: no target analyte peaks above the MDL.
- Duplicate RPD: ≤ 20% [@usepa8081b].


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                  | Container                       | Disposal Method       |
|:----------------------------|:--------------------------------|:----------------------|
| Spent solvents and rinses   | Halogenated or non-halogenated jug (as appropriate) | EH&S pickup |
| Used septa, liners, vials   | Solid chemical waste            | Hazardous waste       |
| Expired pesticide standards | Hazardous waste container       | EH&S pickup           |


## Maintenance

- **Daily:** Replace septum; inspect liner.
- **Weekly:** Check gas trap indicators; verify carrier gas pressure.
- **As needed:** Trim or replace the analytical column if baseline
  degradation or retention time shifts persist [@mcnair2019].
- **Annually:** Full instrument preventive maintenance per manufacturer
  schedule.

## Training Record

Training is documented in the lab training log. Before working
independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Observe a trained operator perform the procedure
3. Perform the procedure under supervision
4. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
